summary: The filed probe returned a decisive receipt and this turn converts the source reading on @timeoutnow_campaign_chain into a measured account. CheckRun 96687fc34bdf45de9237914e30828d38 ran the chain end to end: follower 2 held a live leader context after the leader's heartbeat (index 63, lead_after 1, leader serving at term 2); an ordinary campaign's pre-vote was withheld under that lease (index 64, granted false — the control holds, so the later grant is not a follower answering everyone); then a peer-form MsgTimeoutNow carrying the follower's own term was accepted with an empty step error and moved it to StateCandidate at term 3 (index 65, transfer_context true on both vote requests it produced); the incumbent leader, still inside its lease at term 2, responded and granted the vote and became a follower at term 3 (index 66, responded true, granted true); and the campaign won, leaving node 2 StateLeader at term 3 with two external grants while node 1 stayed a follower (indices 67, 68). So the CheckQuorum lease can be skipped using only message types that legitimately travel the network and only legal field values — no forged local-only type, no unset term anywhere — which is a stronger statement about the lease's strength than the classification finding this run already measured. The judgment does not move: the trigger still requires a sender that is not the leader, both producers of MsgTimeoutNow are leader-side call sites, a superseded former leader's trigger carries an older term and is discarded before the follower path, isUpToDate still guards the vote, and no statement in the snapshot asks a receiver to check the sender against its own r.lead — so the question is recorded as violated with the defect claim refuted, and the interpretation keeps its citation of the marker knowledge entry, now with the receipt-specific assertion. One honest caveat I recorded rather than papered over: two of the four comparisons scored incomplete because of a wiring fault of mine — the admission alias is bound to a node-2 event while the incumbent's events carry node 1, and both nodes' final states share one event name — so the incumbent's grant and node 1's final state are cited from the raw events at indices 66 and 68, and the limitations state the per-node alias fix a future run should apply before re-measuring. Submission validates with execution_requested=false, and no execution is left uncited.
